_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Battery Selection Program Report
summary: The Battery Selection Program Report provides information on military systems, sub-systems, support equipment, and facilities battery requirements to control the proliferation of batteries.
use_relationship:
The purpose of this Data Item Description (DID) is to provide information on military systems, sub-systems, support equipment, and facilities battery requirements. This information will be used to control the proliferation of batteries.
This DID is applicable to the acquisition of systems, subsystems, support equipment, and facilities.
This DID contains the format, content, and intended use information for the product resulting for the work task described in the contract SOW.
This DID supersedes DI-MGMT-80772.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Format.
preparation_instructions.content: The information shall be provided in letter format on 8 1/2 inch by 11-inch paper.

children.title: Information can be provided as enclosures with data presented in tabular or graphical format.
This DID contains the format and content preparation instructions for the data product generated by the specific and discrete task requirement as delineated in the contract.
This DID is applicable to the acquisition of systems, sub-systems, support equipment, and facilities.
It is not intended that all the requirements contained herein should be applied to every program (development or non-development) or program phase.
children.content: However, it shall be required for the acquisition of military systems, sub-systems, equipment, and facilities, which will contain batteries.

children.title: This DID will be most effective in the concept/development phase of the acquisition process.
Portions of this DID are subject to tailoring depending upon the program phase in which it is applied in the solicitation/contract, item being procured, and type battery being used.
If a Military Specification battery is being used, only paragraph 3.8.2.9 applies.
General.
children.content: The battery information provided shall document in detail the following requirements:

children.title: The function that the battery provides to system, sub-system, support equipment of facility (i.e. start, emergency, primary source, etc.).
Design and expected battery performance.
Environmental conditions the battery must survive and provide specification performance.
Shelf life and charging system data.
Content Requirements.
Introductory information:
Name of the system, sub-system, support equipment, or facility.
Contractors name, address, telephone number, and cognizant individual.
A brief description of system, equipment or facility.
Purpose and function of battery (i.e. start, emergency, primary source of power etc.).
Battery information:
Dimensions (metric).
children.content: Attach drawing or sketch if available. Include the dimensions with and without connector for the dimension where pertinent.

children.title: Weight (metric).
Voltages the battery must supply.
Current each voltage section must supply.
children.content: Provide a battery current profile for each voltage section if battery current changes with time.

children.title: For equipment utilizing batteries to perform a start function, provide the following start information:
Start current required vs. time.
Maximum and minimum potential allowed before and during start.
Identify ampere-hours removed from the battery during the preparation for start.
For equipment utilizing batteries to perform an emergency function, provide following emergency information:
Identify typical battery loading during emergency.
The required operating time during emergency loading.
Identify how cells in the battery are connected (series, parallel, or series-parallel).
Electrochemistry (i.e. lead-acid, nickel-cadmium, lithium, etc.).
Identify battery Military specification, military specification sheet, and their dates.
Identify battery commercial specification and date.
children.content: Also, identify the commercial battery part number.

children.title: Rechargeable or non-rechargeable battery.
Number of cells in the battery.
Battery capacity measured in ampere-hours at the C-Rate and 25 degrees C.
Cell information:
children.content: (applicable if only an individual cell is used).

children.title: Dimensions (metric).
children.content: Attach a drawing or sketch if available. Include dimensions with and without connector for the dimension where pertinent.

children.title: Voltage the cell must supply.
The current the cell must provide.
children.content: If the current changes with time, provide a copy of the current profile.

children.title: Type of cell connection (terminal post, recessed threaded stud, tab, etc.).
Electrochemistry.
American National Standards Institute (ANSI) size designation (A, AA, C, D, etc.)
Military specification, specification sheet, and their publication dates.
Commercial specification and commercial part number.
Rechargeable or non-rechargeable.
Cell capacity measured in ampere-hours at the C-Rate and 25 degrees C.
Environmental Information:
Shock levels operating, non-operating, and crash safety.
Vibration levels sine and random, both operating and non-operating.
Maximum high temperature operating and non-operating.
Maximum low temperature operating and non-operating.
Shelf life at 25 degrees C and maximum high temperature non-operating.
Service life at maximum low temperature operating, 25 degrees C, and maximum high temperature operating.
System Information:
Number of batteries identified in paragraphs 3.8.2 or cells identified in paragraph 3.8.3 are in the equipment.
Type of charging method used (i.e. constant voltage, constant current etc.).
For equipment containing chargers, provide the following charging information:
If a constant charge method is used, identify the number of charge steps, current of each charge step and logic (voltage or time) for starting or ending each charge step.
children.content: Justify why this type of charge is required.

children.title: If a constant potential charge method is used identify the voltage the charge will be set at and indicate if it is adjustable.
